result: Topbp1B5/B5 mice are viable with normal body mass and no ionizing radiation sensitivity, but display male-specific infertility with reduced testis size, complete absence of spermatozoa, increased apoptotic spermatocytes, and arrest at pachynema without progression to diplonema.
evaluation: All reviewers affirm the core phenotype of the Topbp1B5/B5 mouse model. Reviewer 1 states the evidence supporting 'defective maintenance of meiotic sex chromosome inactivation is solid,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the generation of a mouse model with a very uncommon phenotype' as a main strength. No reviewer challenges these basic characterization findings.

result: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes display normal pachytene entry, no gross defects in chromosome synapsis (with normal SYCP1/SYCP3 and HORMAD1/HORMAD2 patterns), reach mid-pachynema (H1t positive), and form a morphologically normal sex body.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognize this as a key distinguishing feature. Reviewer 1 describes the phenotype as 'defective MSCI maintenance but normal sex body formation' and notes it 'differs from that of a previous TOPBP1 null allele.' Reviewer 3 emphasizes 'despite a proper morphological formation of the sex body,' indicating acceptance of these findings.

result: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs show no sensitivity to hydroxyurea or phleomycin, can activate DDR signaling (phosphorylation of CHK1, CHK2, RPA2, KAP1), recruit MDC1 to γH2AX-marked DSB foci, and show no increased micronuclei.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these somatic cell findings. The overall assessment that the mutation is a 'separation of function' affecting meiosis but not somatic DDR is accepted by all reviewers, with Reviewer 1 noting the study 'describes a TOPBP1 separation of function mutation.'

result: The B5 mutations disrupt TOPBP1 binding to BLM and 53BP1, and result in reduced protein levels of Flag-TOPBP1-B5 compared to wild-type.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the biochemical characterization of the B5 mutation. Reviewer 1 notes 'Additional defects in CHK phosphorylation and SETX localization are also described,' implicitly accepting the molecular characterization. No reviewer questions the interaction data.

result: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes display normal DNA DSB repair (γH2AX confined to XY, RAD51 only on XY at mid-pachytene), normal TOPBP1 localization to XY chromosomes, normal localization of ATR/BRCA1/MDC1/53BP1, and mostly normal ATR signaling markers (pMDC1 T4, pCHK1 S345, pHORMAD2).
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings as part of the overall characterization showing separation of MSCI from other meiotic functions. Reviewer 3 notes the study shows 'despite a proper morphological formation of the sex body and the incorporation of most canonical MSCI markers,' indicating acceptance of the normal DDR marker localization.

result: Phosphorylation of CHK1 on S317 is significantly decreased in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, but this defect is unlikely to cause the observed infertility based on comparison to Chek1 CKO phenotypes.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly mentions 'Additional defects in CHK phosphorylation' as part of the study's findings, accepting this observation. The interpretation that it is not causal is not challenged by any reviewer.

result: Phosphoproteomic analysis reveals ATR signaling is not drastically impaired in Topbp1B5/B5 testes, but SETX phosphorylation (including at S/T-Q sites) is reduced and SETX spreading to XY chromatin loops is significantly decreased.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'Additional defects in CHK phosphorylation and SETX localization are also described' as part of the study's findings. Reviewer 2 states 'the authors found reduced phosphorylation of a DNA/RNA helicase, Sentaxin, and decreased localization of the protein to the X-Y sex body,' explicitly affirming these results. Reviewer 3 mentions the study shows 'likely due to a defective phosphorylation of the helicase SETX.'

result: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes form a sex body of grossly normal appearance with normal patterns of sex body markers (CHD4, SUMO, USP7), normal chromatin marks (H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me3, H4K16ac, H4ac, H2AK116ub, H3K4me1), and proper exclusion of RNA Pol2.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently recognize normal sex body formation as a key finding. Reviewer 1 describes 'defective MSCI maintenance but normal sex body formation' and Reviewer 3 notes 'despite a proper morphological formation of the sex body and the incorporation of most canonical MSCI markers.' The extensive chromatin mark analysis is not challenged.

result: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals Topbp1B5/B5 testes contain only early spermatocyte populations, can initiate MSCI with robust but incomplete X chromosome silencing, but show increased X and Y gene expression in late spermatocytes including spermatocyte-toxic genes (Zfy1, Zfy2) and other MSCI marker genes (Kdm6a, Lamp2, Zfx, Uba1y, Rhox13, Scml2).
evaluation: All reviewers affirm the transcriptomic evidence for MSCI defects. Reviewer 2 states 'the authors also found decreased repression of several genes on the sex chromosomes in the male mice' and notes 'the works including phospho-proteomics and single-cell RNA sequencing with lots of data have been done with great care and most of the results are convincing.' The Editor states 'The evidence supporting the conclusion that the mutants display defective maintenance of meiotic sex chromosome inactivation is solid.'

result: During the SP2 to SP3 transition, 74 genes in Topbp1B5/B5 versus 4 in wild-type exhibit reduced silencing, while 134 genes show unaltered silencing and only 24 show increased silencing in Topbp1B5/B5 (compared to 43 unaltered and 185 increased in wild-type). The severity of silencing defects correlates with pre-leptotene RNA levels, with highly expressed genes showing more severe defects.
evaluation: While reviewers accept the overall MSCI defect, Reviewer 1 specifically states 'The study claims that MSCI is initiated but not maintained in the mutant. I think alternative hypotheses are possible,' suggesting uncertainty about the interpretation of the temporal dynamics of silencing. The detailed gene-by-gene analysis is not explicitly discussed by reviewers.

result: The Topbp1B5/B5 mouse provides a unique model uncoupling MSCI from sex body formation, representing the first DDR mutant that separates XY silencing from sex body formation and the first mutation impairing TOPBP1's meiotic silencing function without severely disturbing synapsis and sex body formation.
evaluation: All reviewers recognize this as the key conceptual advance. The Editor states 'This important study reports a new mutant mouse line' and emphasizes the novelty. Reviewer 1 describes it as 'a TOPBP1 separation of function mutation, resulting in defective MSCI maintenance but normal sex body formation' and notes 'The phenotype differs from that of a previous TOPBP1 null allele.' Reviewer 3 highlights 'the generation of a mouse model with a very uncommon phenotype' as a main strength.

result: In Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, MLH1 foci are significantly increased while MLH3 foci numbers do not differ significantly from wild-type.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these crossover marker findings. The data are presented as part of the comprehensive characterization showing normal progression through pachynema, which reviewers accept.

result: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes exhibit subtle defects/delays in γH2AX spreading on the PAR and pericentromeric regions, accounting for 56% of mid-pachytene cells.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this finding. It is presented as a minor defect consistent with the overall phenotype of largely normal sex body formation with MSCI maintenance defects, which reviewers accept.
